newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina seeks amnesty for illegal labor - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentina seeks amnesty for illegal labor - report.

text.p: The Argentine government is planning a blanket amnesty for employers with illegal workers, Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa said in Tuesday's edition of the local daily Clarin.
Caro Figueroa said the government backed a draft law for an amnesty which would also benefit self-employed workers who do not pay income and pension taxes.
"We will support the bill if it guarantees that the situation of workers hired off the books will be normalized with no sanctions to employers," the minister told Clarin.
But he said the government would refuse to recognize workers' rights to backdated social security contributions, as called for in the bill drafted by two legislators of the ruling Peronist Party.

"(Workers) will have to convince employers to pay the contributions for the years they worked illegally, which I realize is very hard to do," Caro Figueroa said. "The amnesty will clear the record for the future, but it doesn't solve the problem of the past."
The illegal workforce is officially estimated at around four million people, depriving the government of $8.0 billion in yearly revenues, Clarin said.
